own_solution.law: P = F . v = T v cos(theta)
assumptions: sled moves horizontally at the stated speed
rope tension 40 N along the rope at 30 degrees

TF8CB.regime: rope intact while tension < breaking tension; 40 N < 210 N

T8FA9.regime: rope intact while tension < breaking tension; 40 N < 210 N

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: For the R sentences (T7A7D, TAAB5) the text does not say that the tension stays 40 N and the speed stays 3 m/s after the tilt; with ground friction, keeping constant speed at 47 degrees would generally need a different tension, so the answer 81.84 W rests on reading the stated tension and speed as still holding.

notes: Base: 40*3*cos30 = 103.92 W. Tilted to 47 degrees with T = 40 N and v = 3 m/s as stated: 120*cos47 = 120*0.68200 = 81.84 W. I take the literal reading that all stated values (40 N, 3 m/s) still hold, which gives a unique answer; I rate the gap medium rather than high because no competing determinate answer is available from the given data. Duration of pulling (55 s) fixes only the work, not the power; I class it C (P = W/t), D would also be defensible. Variants: 17 degrees in T7A7D/TD53D/TAAB5/T4A60; 'a little' in TB8F6/T3D43; 210 N in TF8CB/T8FA9; 55 s in T012E/TFC2B. Consistent. T7A7D's 'then' leaves ambiguous whether the question refers to before or after the tilt; read as after.
